subject.title: CLI startup preflight can corrupt the live state DB while a gateway is running — health-check commands caused "database disk image is malformed" (2026.6.6, macOS); vanilla SQLite control does NOT reproduce

question: Should OpenClaw make shared-state access RPC-first/no-maintenance for CLI health surfaces, enforce a stricter gateway single-writer lease, or require forensic harness proof before choosing the DB ownership policy?
rationale: The current source path confirms mutable CLI-side shared DB open/checkpoint behavior, but the permanent fix changes ownership boundaries for gateway observability, doctor migrations, plugin-state probes, and operator recovery.

options.title: RPC-first plus no-maintenance CLI
options.body: Status, health, and stability should ask the running gateway first, and fallback file opens while the gateway is active should be read-only with no journal or checkpoint pragmas.

options.title: Single-writer gateway lease
options.body: The gateway should own the shared state DB write and maintenance lease, with non-gateway processes failing closed or routing through gateway APIs for writes and maintenance.

options.title: Forensic harness first
options.body: Pause implementation until the reporter's corrupt DB bundle and a native runtime harness confirm the exact helper/runtime interaction under load.

recommendation.title: RPC-first plus no-maintenance CLI
recommendation.body: Status, health, and stability should ask the running gateway first, and fallback file opens while the gateway is active should be read-only with no journal or checkpoint pragmas.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision cuts across the DB-first runtime-state architecture and gateway/CLI ownership boundary introduced by the SQLite refactor.
